preamble: Backing and rounding of the open-mid back unrounded vowel [ʌ] to [ɔ]. In the Northern Cities Vowel Shift of Inland Northern American English, the STRUT vowel /ʌ/ moves from a central or back position toward a very far back [ɔ], so that bus sounds more like boss to speakers without the shift; Wikipedia gives its realization as [ʌ~ɔ] (bus, flood, what). STRUT backing was first reported in 1986 and is one of the later stages of the shift: it follows the lowering of THOUGHT /ɔ/ and the backing and lowering of DRESS /ɛ/, each vowel moving into the space left by the previous one. Eckert describes the same movement in the Detroit suburbs, where the vowel of lunch and tough shifts towards that of all and caught. The change is a regional, ongoing development within one variety of American English; in the California Vowel Shift STRUT moves forward instead.

examples.to: toward [ɔ]; bus sounds more like boss
examples.note: Wikipedia gives the Inland Northern realization of /ʌ/ as [ʌ~ɔ], with the examples bus, flood, what.

examples.to: toward the vowel of all, caught; fun sounds more like fawn
examples.note: Eckert (Detroit suburbs): the vowel in lunch, tough shifts towards the vowel in all, caught.
